verdicts.why: The set-union sense is a mathematical term that names a construction and takes no side on it.
Names an entrance room; a formal or architectural register but no approval or dismissal of the room.
An anatomical term for a cavity; purely descriptive.
Names liveliness of spirit; the quality is pleasant by referent, but the word itself describes rather than praises (the 'sweet' in the sentence does the approving).
General activity and motion, described without judgement.
The craft of making cartoons; a plain technical name.
The act of enlivening something; descriptive of the activity, no attitude beyond the meaning.
The state of being alive, a plain condition-name.
Capacity to survive and grow is a property, named neutrally.
A body part named plainly.
A weapon named plainly; the referent may be grim but the word takes no side.
A part of a chair; purely descriptive.
A projection resembling an arm; shape description only.
A division of an organization; neutral structural term.
A sleeve; plain garment-part name.
A division of an organization or subject; neutral structural term.
A part of a plant, named plainly.
A tributary stream; geographic description only.
A part of a forked shape; purely descriptive.
An outgrowth or consequence of development, stated without judgement.
A projection resembling an arm; shape description only.
The limitation ('satisfy in a limited way') is the meaning itself, and 'content oneself with' is if anything more neutral than its neighbour 'settle for', which is the one that sneers.
To make someone content names a pleasant result plainly; no attitude beyond the meaning.
Speaking in someone's defence is described without the speaker's own approval or contempt attached.
Protecting against attack is a plain action-name; no judgement of the defender or the attacked.
